# Functional investment along the vent gradient

The community-level result says environment structures both profiles but explains a modest share of either. *What functional profiles shift across the vent sites?* Pool by functional categories (COG) and KEGG categories to look for patterns. 

Hypothesis: we have warmer, lower Mg, more acidic vent fluid. This should reflect or be translated into some change in growth signatures at the gene level. Examples from COG:
* translation, ribosome biogenesis
* protein folding and turnover
* energy conversion

*Do we see evidence of any changes in growth parameters for microeukaryotes?* Do we see anything along a specific environmental gradient. 

_Using COG, KEGG, and pfam_:

1. **COG functional categories**: Every KO-annotated transcript carries a COG letter from the same eggNOG annotation used throughout, so the category composition is complete. WIll be broader than other inquires below; COG J is translation machinery broadly (ribosomal proteins *and* tRNA synthetases, initiation and elongation factors), not ribosomes alone.

2. **KEGG BRITE level-B categories**: Same design as COG, but each KO is placed in KEGG functional categories (_Translation; Folding, sorting and degradation; Energy metabolism_) from BRITE `ko00001` hierarchy. KEGG groupings tend to resolve microeukaryote function better than COG letters. The cost is coverage: only KOs with a BRITE level-B assignment contribute, and the mapped share of expression is reported.

3. **PFAM-matched panels** (sensitivity). Sharper a priori sets — ribosomal proteins, chaperones, oxidative-phosphorylation complexes — matched by regex against the `PFAMs` column. Higher resolution, but the membership is a text match, so the chunk prints every PFAM name it caught for auditing.

All tiers use the same 13 vent units, the same transcripts as the dbRDA, and the same retained predictors.

> **Metatranscriptome abundances are compositional**, so "reduced investment in translation" means a smaller share of expression, not fewer transcripts per cell. The rclr transform makes that explicit. Interprte as "relative"


## Configure the functional tiers

```{r growth-config}
# COG functional categories (Galperin et al. 2021, Nucleic Acids Res 49:D274-D281). Single letters, as eggNOG-mapper emits them.
COG_DESCRIPTIONS <- c(
  J = "Translation, ribosomal structure and biogenesis", # USE THIS
  A = "RNA processing and modification",
  K = "Transcription",
  L = "Replication, recombination and repair",
  B = "Chromatin structure and dynamics",
  D = "Cell cycle control, cell division, chromosome partitioning",
  Y = "Nuclear structure",
  V = "Defense mechanisms",
  T = "Signal transduction mechanisms",
  M = "Cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis",
  N = "Cell motility",
  Z = "Cytoskeleton",
  W = "Extracellular structures",
  U = "Intracellular trafficking, secretion, vesicular transport",
  O = "Post-translational modification, protein turnover, chaperones", # USE THIS
  X = "Mobilome: prophages, transposons",
  C = "Energy production and conversion", # USE THIS
  G = "Carbohydrate transport and metabolism",
  E = "Amino acid transport and metabolism",
  F = "Nucleotide transport and metabolism",
  H = "Coenzyme transport and metabolism",
  I = "Lipid transport and metabolism",
  P = "Inorganic ion transport and metabolism",
  Q = "Secondary metabolites biosynthesis, transport, catabolism",
  R = "General function prediction only",
  S = "Function unknown")

COG_SELECT <- c("J", "O", "C")

# PFAMs AUDIT
PFAM_PANELS <- c(
  ribosomal_protein = "ribosomal_|ribosomal protein",
  chaperone = "hsp[0-9]|cpn[0-9]|cpn60|dnaj|grpe|prefoldin|chaperon|tcp1|clpb",
  oxidative_phosphoryl = "^cox[0-9]|cytochrom|atp-synt|complex1|nadhdh|oxidored_q|ubiq_cyt|ucr|qcr")

# Permutations for the category / panel correlations.
N_PERM_CAT <- 9999

# KO map BRITE hierarchy `ko00001`
KEGG_BRITE_FILE <- "data/external/ko00001.keg"
# rm animal-centric (Organismal Systems, Human Diseases) and non-pathways
KEGG_EXCLUDE_A  <- c("09150", "09160", "09180", "09190")
# KEGG level B:
## 09122 Translation
## 09123 Folding, sorting and degradation
## 09102 Energy metabolism
KEGG_SELECT    <- c("09122", "09123", "09102")
```

## One Spearman helper for both tiers

Spearman rho per column of `z` against `x`, with a permutation value `x` is shuffled across units, so the null value preserves each feature's own distribution and only breaks its link to the variable. Returns rho and a two-sided permutation p; BH correction is applied later, across the whole reported family.

```{r growth-spearman-fn}
spearman_perm <- function(z, x, n_perm = N_PERM_CAT) {
  stopifnot(nrow(z) == length(x))
# A feature with the same value in every unit (e.g. a category absent from all of them) has no ranks to correlate and would return NaN. Drop those and say so.
  keep <- apply(z, 2, \(col) stats::sd(col) > 0)
  if (any(!keep)) {
    message(glue::glue("  dropped {sum(!keep)} zero-variance feature(s): ","{paste(colnames(z)[!keep], collapse = ', ')}"))
  }
  z <- z[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  if (ncol(z) == 0) stop("No variable features left to correlate.", call. = FALSE) #if none
  ##
  rz <- scale(apply(z, 2, rank))
  rx <- as.numeric(scale(rank(x)))
  n  <- length(x)
  rho <- as.vector(crossprod(rz, rx)) / (n - 1)
  ##
  perm <- replicate(n_perm, sample(rx)) # units x n_perm
  null <- abs(crossprod(rz, perm)) / (n - 1)  # features x n_perm
  ## form table
  tibble::tibble(
    feature = colnames(z),
    rho     = rho,
    p_perm  = (1 + rowSums(null >= abs(rho))) / (1 + n_perm))
}
```

## Tier 1 — COG

A transcript carrying several COG letters (e.g. `"BDLTU"`) needs to split scaledTPM across them (same as `prep_paired()`). Categories are then summed per biological unit with the same zero-aware mean (`sum / n_reps`), and the units x category matrix is rclr-transformed. All 26 categories are kept, including `R` and `S` (uninformative but real expression); can't drop, because we need CLR reference. 

```{r growth-cog-matrix}
#| message: true
if (!"COG_category" %in% names(paired_mod)) {
  stop("`COG_category` is not in the annotation table. This section needs the eggNOG ",
       "COG column carried from long_frenemies_annot_tax.", call. = FALSE)
}

# What are the counts. 02 carries SEQ_ID; fall back to SequenceID, and if neither survived, count the row.

TX_ID <- c("SEQ_ID", "SequenceID")[c("SEQ_ID", "SequenceID") %in% names(paired_mod)][1]
if (is.na(TX_ID)) {
  message("No SEQ_ID/SequenceID column: n_transcripts counts transcript x KO rows, ",
          "not distinct transcripts.")
}

cog_split <- paired_mod |>
  filter(vent_bin == "Vent",
                !is.na(COG_category), !COG_category %in% c("", "-")) |>
  mutate(.txid = if (!is.na(TX_ID)) .data[[TX_ID]] else row_number(),
                n_cog = nchar(COG_category)) |>
  separate_longer_position(COG_category, width = 1) |>
  rename(cog = COG_category) |>
  mutate(scaledTPM = scaledTPM / n_cog)

cog_by_unit <- cog_split |>
  group_by(unit = .data[[UNIT_COL]], n_reps, cog) |>
  summarise(tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / dplyr::first(n_reps), .groups = "drop") |>
  select(-n_reps)

cog_mat <- cog_by_unit |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = cog, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("unit") |>
  as.matrix()

# align rows to the predictor table used by the dbRDA
cog_mat <- cog_mat[env_model$unit, , drop = FALSE]
cog_z <- rclr_transform(cog_mat)

# Categories must actually be present, or the prediction cannot be tested. Filter before cog_support, which reads COG_SELECT

COG_SELECT <- COG_SELECT[COG_SELECT %in% colnames(cog_mat)]
if (!length(COG_SELECT)) {
  stop("None of the a priori COG categories (J/O/C) are present in the vent data.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

# how much each category rests on -- the reader should see this before any rho
cog_support <- cog_split |>
  summarise(n_transcripts = n_distinct(.txid), 
            n_kos = n_distinct(ko_id),
            total_tpm = sum(scaledTPM),
            .by = cog) |>
  mutate(pct_tpm = round(100 * total_tpm / sum(total_tpm), 2),
                description = unname(COG_DESCRIPTIONS[cog]),
                a_priori= cog %in% COG_SELECT) |>
  arrange(desc(total_tpm))

message(glue::glue("{nrow(cog_mat)} vent units x {ncol(cog_mat)} COG categories | ",
                   "a priori present: {paste(COG_SELECT, collapse = ', ')}"))
cog_support |> dplyr::select(cog, description, a_priori, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

> **Check first.** If `J`, `O` or `C` has only a few KOs, the slow-growth test has little behind it and should be reported as inconclusive rather than negative. `S` (function unknown) carrying a large share of TPM is normal for protist metatranscriptomes and is worth one sentence in the results.

```{r growth-cog-corr}
#| message: true
set.seed(params$seed)

cog_gradient <- purrr::map_dfr(env_keep, \(v)
  spearman_perm(cog_z, env_model[[v]]) |>
    mutate(variable = v, .before = 1)) |>
  rename(cog = feature) |>
  # BH across the whole reported family (every category x every variable)
  mutate(q_bh = stats::p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH")) |>
  left_join(select(cog_support, cog, description, n_kos, n_transcripts,
                                 pct_tpm, a_priori),
                   by = "cog") |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(rho < 0, "decreases", "increases"),
                significant = q_bh <= params$fdr_alpha) |>
  arrange(variable, rho)

# The pre-specified test, stated on its own so it cannot be lost in the full table.
cog_apriori_result <- cog_gradient |>
  filter(a_priori) |>
  select(variable, cog, description, n_kos, pct_tpm, rho, p_perm, q_bh, direction) |>
  mutate(across(c(rho, p_perm, q_bh), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  arrange(variable, cog)

cog_apriori_result |> print(n = Inf)
```

> **Read the three a priori rows against the prediction.** The slow-growth reading needs `J`, `O` and `C` all negative with temperature. Two of three, or a negative rho that does not clear BH, is a too weak or not well established

```{r growth-cog-table}
#| message: true
cog_gradient |>
  filter(significant) |>
  select(variable, cog, description, rho, q_bh, a_priori) |>
  mutate(across(c(rho, q_bh), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  print(n = Inf)

message(glue::glue(
  "{sum(cog_gradient$significant)} of {nrow(cog_gradient)} category x variable tests ",
  "clear BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}"))
```

### Figure: functional investment vs. the environmental gradient

Top row: every COG category's rank correlation with each retained variable, sorted by
effect for temperature. Filled points clear BH; the three a priori categories are labelled
and coloured. Bottom row: the a priori categories' rclr values against temperature, one
panel each, so the reader sees the actual 13 points rather than only a coefficient.
The scatter axes carry raw temperature (°C) for readability; the test is rank-based, so
z-scoring the predictor does not change rho.

```{r growth-cog-figure}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| warning: false
select_color <- "#346D6E"   # _brand.yml deep-teal

cog_order <- cog_gradient |>
  filter(variable == "TEMP") |>
  arrange(rho) |>
  pull(cog)

p_rho <- cog_gradient |>
  mutate(cog = factor(cog, levels = cog_order),# Follow temp
                variable = factor(variable, levels = env_keep)) |>
  ggplot(aes(rho, cog)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey70") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = rho, 
                   yend = cog, color = select_color), 
               linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = select_color, shape = significant), size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = select_color, `FALSE` = "grey55"),
                               labels = c(`TRUE` = "a priori (J/O/C)", `FALSE` = "context"),
                               name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21),
                              labels = c(`TRUE` = glue::glue("BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}"),
                                         `FALSE` = "n.s."),
                              name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = expression(Spearman~rho), y = "COG category",
                title = "Functional category vs. environment, all 13 vent units") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

apriori_points <- tibble::as_tibble(cog_z[, COG_SELECT, drop = FALSE],
                                    rownames = "unit") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(COG_SELECT), names_to = "cog", values_to = "rclr") |>
  left_join(select(env_vent, unit, field, TEMP), by = "unit") |>
  left_join(cog_gradient |> filter(variable == "TEMP") |>
                     select(cog, rho, q_bh), by = "cog") |>
  mutate(panel = glue::glue(
    "COG {cog}: {stringr::str_trunc(unname(COG_DESCRIPTIONS[cog]), 34)}\nrho = {round(rho, 2)}, q = {signif(q_bh, 2)}"))

p_scatter <- ggplot(apriori_points, aes(TEMP, rclr)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4,
                       color = select_color, formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = field), shape = 21, size = 2.6,
                      color = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_field, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Temperature (\u00b0C)", y = "rclr (category share)",
                caption = paste("Line is a least-squares guide only; the test is the",
                                "rank correlation above.")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                 strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

patchwork::wrap_plots(p_rho, p_scatter, ncol = 1, heights = c(1.3, 1))
```

## Tier 1b — KEGG categories
Same design as Tier 1 with KEGG BRITE level-B categories in place of COG letters.

* **Mapping.** KO to level-B category from `data/external/ko00001.keg`. The excluded top-level classes are set in `KEGG_EXCLUDE_A`; print `brite_map` to see exactly what remains.
* **Multi-category KOs.** A KO placed in *n* distinct level-B categories splits its scaledTPM equally across them, the same mass-conserving rule used for multi-KO transcripts and multi-letter COG codes. A KO in two pathways of the *same* level-B category counts once there.
* **Coverage.** KOs with no retained level-B category drop out, so the composition is over *mapped* expression only. The chunk prints the mapped share of vent TPM. Report it.
* **Family for BH.** Category x variable tests within this tier are corrected as one family, separately from COG.


```{r growth-kegg-map}
#| message: true
#| warning: false
if (!file.exists(KEGG_BRITE_FILE)) {
  stop("`", KEGG_BRITE_FILE, "` not found. Download the KEGG BRITE KO hierarchy once, e.g.\n",
       "  curl -o ", KEGG_BRITE_FILE, " \"https://rest.kegg.jp/get/br:ko00001\"\n",
       "then re-run.", call. = FALSE)
}

# >SKH: shared parser R/read_brite.R (same map 06 uses; replaces the inline copy, 2026-10-12)
brite_map <- read_brite_level_b(KEGG_BRITE_FILE, exclude_a = KEGG_EXCLUDE_A) |>
  select(ko_id, kegg_a, kegg, description, n_cat)

# The a priori ids must exist in the file, and their names are printed so the id -> name match can be checked by eye.
stopifnot(all(KEGG_SELECT %in% brite_map$kegg))
brite_map |>
  filter(kegg %in% KEGG_SELECT) |>
  distinct(kegg, description) |>
  print()

message(glue::glue(
  "{n_distinct(brite_map$ko_id)} KOs in {n_distinct(brite_map$kegg)} level-B categories | ",
  "{n_distinct(brite_map$ko_id[brite_map$n_cat > 1])} KOs sit in more than one"))
```

Builds the units x KEGG-category matrix with the same unit averaging and rclr as the COG tier.

```{r growth-kegg-matrix}
#| message: true
# Only the columns needed, before the many-to-many join, to keep memory down.
kegg_split <- paired_mod |>
  filter(vent_bin == "Vent") |>
  transmute(unit = .data[[UNIT_COL]], n_reps, ko_id, scaledTPM,
                   .txid = if (!is.na(TX_ID)) .data[[TX_ID]] else row_number()) |>
  inner_join(brite_map, by = "ko_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(scaledTPM = scaledTPM / n_cat)

# Mass conservation: splitting across categories must not create or lose TPM.
vent_ko_tpm <- paired_mod |> filter(vent_bin == "Vent")
mapped_tpm  <- sum(vent_ko_tpm$scaledTPM[vent_ko_tpm$ko_id %in% brite_map$ko_id])
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sum(kegg_split$scaledTPM), mapped_tpm)))
message(glue::glue(
  "{round(100 * mapped_tpm / sum(vent_ko_tpm$scaledTPM), 1)}% of KO-annotated vent TPM ",
  "maps to a retained KEGG level-B category"))

kegg_mat <- kegg_split |>
  summarise(tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / first(n_reps), .by = c(unit, n_reps, kegg)) |>
  select(-n_reps) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = kegg, values_from = tpm, values_fill = 0) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("unit") |>
  as.matrix()

kegg_mat <- kegg_mat[env_model$unit, , drop = FALSE]
kegg_z   <- rclr_transform(kegg_mat)

# A priori categories must be present, or the prediction cannot be tested.
KEGG_SELECT <- KEGG_SELECT[KEGG_SELECT %in% colnames(kegg_mat)]
if (!length(KEGG_SELECT)) {
  stop("None of the a priori KEGG categories are present in the vent data.", call. = FALSE)
}

kegg_support <- kegg_split |>
  summarise(n_transcripts = n_distinct(.txid),
                   n_kos = n_distinct(ko_id),
                   total_tpm = sum(scaledTPM),
                   .by = c(kegg, description)) |>
  mutate(pct_tpm  = round(100 * total_tpm / sum(total_tpm), 2),
                a_priori = kegg %in% KEGG_SELECT) |>
  arrange(desc(total_tpm))

message(glue::glue("{nrow(kegg_mat)} vent units x {ncol(kegg_mat)} KEGG categories | ",
                   "a priori present: {paste(KEGG_SELECT, collapse = ', ')}"))
kegg_support |>
  select(kegg, description, a_priori, n_kos, n_transcripts, pct_tpm) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r growth-kegg-corr}
#| message: true
set.seed(params$seed)

kegg_gradient <- purrr::map_dfr(env_keep, \(v)
  spearman_perm(kegg_z, env_model[[v]]) |>
    mutate(variable = v, .before = 1)) |>
  rename(kegg = feature) |>
  # BH across this tier's whole family (every category x every variable)
  mutate(q_bh = stats::p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH")) |>
  left_join(select(kegg_support, kegg, description, n_kos, n_transcripts,
                                 pct_tpm, a_priori),
                   by = "kegg") |>
  mutate(direction   = if_else(rho < 0, "decreases", "increases"),
                significant = q_bh <= params$fdr_alpha) |>
  arrange(variable, rho)

kegg_apriori_result <- kegg_gradient |>
  filter(a_priori) |>
  select(variable, kegg, description, n_kos, pct_tpm, rho, p_perm, q_bh, direction) |>
  mutate(across(c(rho, p_perm, q_bh), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  arrange(variable, kegg)

kegg_apriori_result |> print(n = Inf)

message(glue::glue(
  "{sum(kegg_gradient$significant)} of {nrow(kegg_gradient)} category x variable tests ",
  "clear BH q <= {params$fdr_alpha}"))
```

> **Read the three a priori rows against the prediction**, exactly as for COG: all three negative with temperature supports the slow-growth reading; fewer, or a negative rho that does not clear BH, is "consistent with, but not established by". Where COG and KEGG disagree on direction for the matching category (J vs Translation, O vs Folding/sorting/degradation, C vs Energy metabolism), report both.

## Tier 2 — PFAM-matched panels (sensitivity)

COG J mixes ribosomal proteins with the rest of the translation apparatus, so a decline in
J is not by itself a ribosome result. These three panels are narrower. Membership is a
regex match against `PFAMs`, which is why the matched names are printed: **audit that table
before citing this tier.** A transcript matching two panels counts in both.

Each panel is expressed as its **share of total KO-annotated vent expression** per unit
rather than rclr, because three hand-picked panels do not form a composition. Spearman is
rank-based, so a correlation on the share is identical to one on the log-ratio of panel to
non-panel expression.

```{r growth-pfam-audit}
#| message: true
if (!"PFAMs" %in% names(paired_mod)) {
  stop("`PFAMs` is not in the annotation table; the sensitivity tier cannot run. ",
       "Either carry the eggNOG PFAMs column through 02 or delete this tier.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

# `.by` does not accept renaming, so the unit column is materialized once here.
vent_pfam <- paired_mod |>
  dplyr::filter(vent_bin == "Vent") |>
  dplyr::mutate(unit  = .data[[UNIT_COL]],
                .txid = if (!is.na(TX_ID)) .data[[TX_ID]] else dplyr::row_number())

# Audit on the DISTINCT PFAM strings (a few thousand) rather than every transcript.
pfam_audit <- vent_pfam |>
  dplyr::distinct(PFAMs) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(PFAMs), !PFAMs %in% c("", "-")) |>
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(PFAMs, delim = ",") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pfam = stringr::str_trim(PFAMs)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(pfam) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(panel = names(PFAM_PANELS)) |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(pfam, stringr::regex(PFAM_PANELS[panel],
                                                         ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_pfam = dplyr::n_distinct(pfam),
                   pfams = paste(sort(unique(pfam)), collapse = ", "),
                   .by = panel)

pfam_audit |> dplyr::select(panel, n_pfam) |> print()
purrr::pwalk(pfam_audit, \(panel, n_pfam, pfams)
  message(glue::glue("\n{panel} ({n_pfam} PFAM families):\n  {stringr::str_trunc(pfams, 900)}")))
```

> **Audit gate.** If a panel caught an unrelated family, or caught almost nothing, fix the
> regex in `PFAM_PANELS` or drop that panel. Do not report a panel whose match list you have
> not read.

```{r growth-pfam-corr}
#| message: true
set.seed(params$seed)

unit_total <- vent_pfam |>
  dplyr::summarise(total_tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / dplyr::first(n_reps),
                   .by = c(unit, n_reps)) |>
  dplyr::select(unit, total_tpm)

panel_share <- purrr::imap_dfr(PFAM_PANELS, \(rx, panel_name)
  vent_pfam |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(PFAMs),
                  stringr::str_detect(PFAMs, stringr::regex(rx, ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
    dplyr::summarise(panel_tpm = sum(scaledTPM) / dplyr::first(n_reps),
                     n_transcripts = dplyr::n_distinct(.txid),
                     .by = c(unit, n_reps)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = panel_name) |>
    dplyr::select(-n_reps)) |>
  # Complete against EXPLICIT levels: a panel that matched nothing anywhere would
  # otherwise vanish from the results instead of reporting a zero share.
  tidyr::complete(unit = unit_total$unit, panel = names(PFAM_PANELS),
                  fill = list(panel_tpm = 0, n_transcripts = 0)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(unit_total, by = "unit") |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = panel_tpm / total_tpm)

share_mat <- panel_share |>
  dplyr::select(unit, panel, share) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = panel, values_from = share) |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("unit") |>
  as.matrix()
share_mat <- share_mat[env_model$unit, , drop = FALSE]

panel_gradient <- purrr::map_dfr(env_keep, \(v)
  spearman_perm(share_mat, env_model[[v]]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(variable = v, .before = 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(panel = feature) |>
  dplyr::mutate(q_bh = stats::p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH"),
                direction = dplyr::if_else(rho < 0, "decreases", "increases"),
                significant = q_bh <= params$fdr_alpha) |>
  dplyr::left_join(panel_share |>
                     dplyr::summarise(n_transcripts = sum(n_transcripts),
                                      mean_share = mean(share), .by = panel),
                   by = "panel") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(rho, p_perm, q_bh), \(x) round(x, 4)),
                mean_share = round(mean_share, 4)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(variable, rho)

panel_gradient |>
  dplyr::select(variable, panel, n_transcripts, mean_share, rho, p_perm, q_bh,
                direction, significant) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r growth-pfam-figure}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| warning: false
panel_share |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(env_vent, unit, field, TEMP), by = "unit") |>
  dplyr::left_join(panel_gradient |> dplyr::filter(variable == "TEMP") |>
                     dplyr::select(panel, rho, q_bh), by = "panel") |>
  dplyr::mutate(facet = glue::glue("{panel}\nrho = {rho}, q = {signif(q_bh, 2)}")) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(TEMP, share)) +
  ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4,
                       colour = select_color, formula = y ~ x) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(fill = field), shape = 21, size = 2.6,
                      colour = "grey20") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ facet, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = color_field, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Temperature (\u00b0C)",
                y = "share of vent expression",
                title = "Sensitivity tier: PFAM-matched growth machinery vs. temperature") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8))
```
